title: Accomplice or Corrective? Google and YouTube’s Role in Spreading Conspiracy Theories about Chancellor Candidate Annalena Baerbock during the 2021 German Federal Election
screen_reason: German-language abstract only. It reports a standardised content analysis of n = 8,601 Google and YouTube search results for eight conspiracy-related search terms, and states that on Google 'rund ein Viertel' [about a quarter] of the results support the conspiracy theory. That is a quantitative share of items in a sample judged against the researchers' validated definition of the conspiracy narrative, i.e. a CONTENT estimate. Only one usable value exists; the YouTube result is qualitative ('very few').

estimates.date: around the 2021 German federal election (Bundestagswahl, 26 September 2021); exact collection window not stated in the abstract
estimates.measure_type: % of Google search results (for eight validated conspiracy search terms) that support the Baerbock / 'Great Reset' conspiracy theory
estimates.value_raw: "rund ein Viertel" [about a quarter] of the Google search results; total content-analysed set n = 8,601 search results (Google + YouTube)
estimates.denominator: the Google portion of the n = 8,601 search results content-analysed across Google and YouTube for eight conspiracy-related search terms; the Google-only denominator is NOT given in the abstract
estimates.definition: a search result was counted if it supports ('unterstützt') the conspiracy theory about Annalena Baerbock and the 'Great Reset'
estimates.misinfo_def: "das konspirative Narrativ ... eine Verschwörungstheorie über Annalena Baerbock und den „Great Reset“" [the conspiracy narrative ... a conspiracy theory about Annalena Baerbock and the 'Great Reset']
estimates.n: 8,601 search results (Google + YouTube combined; Google-only n not stated)
estimates.source_quote: In der Hauptstudie zeigt eine standardisierte Inhaltsanalyse der Suchergebnisse (n = 8.601), dass auf Google rund ein Viertel die Verschwörungstheorie unterstützt.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Standardised content analysis by the research team ('standardisierte Inhaltsanalyse'); the conspiracy narrative and its eight search terms were first identified and validated in a preliminary study using investigative digital ethnography on Telegram. No coder-reliability statistics are reported in the abstract.
estimates.moderator_quote: In der Vorstudie werden mittels einer investigativen digitalen Ethnographie das konspirative Narrativ und acht dazugehörige Suchterme auf Telegram identifiziert und validiert.
estimates.notes: ABSTRACT-ONLY extraction, German source. English translation of the source_quote: 'In the main study, a standardised content analysis of the search results (n = 8,601) shows that on Google about a quarter support the conspiracy theory.' Three cautions for the adjudicator: (a) the value is the authors' own verbal approximation ('rund ein Viertel'), not a printed percentage — I have rendered it as 25 with value_kind proportion, but a stricter reading of R8 would refuse it; (b) the denominator n = 8,601 covers BOTH Google and YouTube, so the Google-only base is unknown from the abstract and the row's n is an upper bound; (c) denom_selection = curated is inferred — search-engine result sets are rank-truncated by construction — but the abstract does not state how many results per query were coded. year = 2021 is the election year given in the title/abstract; the exact fieldwork window is not stated.

missed_or_uncertain: YouTube: 'Auf YouTube führten dagegen nur sehr spezifische Suchterme zu (sehr wenigen) verschwörungstheoretischen Inhalten.' [On YouTube, by contrast, only very specific search terms led to (very few) conspiracy-theory contents.] — no number, no denominator, so no YouTube row, even though a full text would almost certainly supply one. If the full text is later obtained, this paper should yield at least two rows (Google, YouTube) with exact per-platform denominators, and probably per-search-term breakdowns. The preliminary Telegram ethnography is qualitative and yields nothing extractable.

rob.design: Two-stage design reported in a German abstract only. Preliminary study: investigative digital ethnography on Telegram to identify and validate the conspiracy narrative and eight associated search terms. Main study: standardised quantitative content analysis of n = 8,601 Google and YouTube search results returned by those terms. No sampling depth, coder count, coder training or intercoder-reliability statistics are reported in the abstract.
rob.item6_quote: In der Vorstudie werden mittels einer investigativen digitalen Ethnographie das konspirative Narrativ und acht dazugehörige Suchterme auf Telegram identifiziert und validiert.
rob.item10_quote: In der Hauptstudie zeigt eine standardisierte Inhaltsanalyse der Suchergebnisse (n = 8.601), dass auf Google rund ein Viertel die Verschwörungstheorie unterstützt.
